scope: latest direct feedback: v17 head with mane, articulated bomber wing roots, v18-inspired blunt nose, knee axes, bomber color refinement
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / mechanical design refinement. EDIT image 1, the full-body orange/ivory combined robot, keeping its powerful thick torso, real enormous closed fists, reinforced forearms, rear-facing train half-shell arm equipment, long tracked drilling legs, tall heroic proportions and accepted hand-drawn KINETIC_CEL rendering. Plain warm ivory background, generously framed square, complete wing tips/crown/hands/feet inside the frame. ONE robot, no text or effects.

Reference 1 is the edit target and overall identity. Reference 2 v17 controls ONLY the preferred HEAD HELMET/crown character; keep the long orange-white mane behind that helmet. Reference 3 v18 controls ONLY a more handsome compact integrated CHEST NOSE shape and knee-drill orientation; do NOT copy its whole trains on shoulders, small fists or short stature.

Make these precise changes:

1. ARTICULATED BOMBER SHOULDERS. Keep the full large swept wings, paired engines and thick bomber center fuselage from image 1. Divide that bomber into THREE clearly separate connected mechanical modules: one central fuselage/cockpit unit mounted rigidly over the chest/back, plus independent left and right wing/nacelle units. At EACH wing root, between the side of the central fuselage and the wing module, show a short visible dark mechanical gap, a substantial circular rotary bearing and orange/steel fork bracket. The core shoulder joint beneath is exposed with clearance, so the arm can rotate/raise without dragging a rigid single airplane across both shoulders. Outer wings and engines belong to the wing modules. Keep the wing roots mechanically supported, not floating or severed. A small difference in wing pitch can show rotation while preserving the powerful wide bomber silhouette. NO unbroken rigid wing plate crossing directly over the core shoulder articulation. Keep all large wing planform area; do not shrink wings back into shoulder spikes.

2. COMPACT BLUNT CHEST NOSE. Replace the long pointed beak cockpit nose with a shorter, wider, well-designed v18-like integrated chest fuselage. A compact faceted canopy close to the upper chest, broad angular orange cheek surfaces and a gently rounded/chamfered blunt lower nose. The frontmost face is a shallow trapezoid, not an acute spear point. It should look like an elegant robust rescue-bomber front, not a train cab, animal beak or large projecting knife. Only ONE cockpit/nose; continuous deep chest volume beneath.

3. HEAD FROM v17, KEEP HAIR. Prefer the compact fierce v17 helmet: angular silver face frame and cheek plates, strong orange brow/central crest and an orderly jagged silver/orange mechanical crown. Keep cyan eyes, orange/white long mane. Replace image 1's over-busy feather-like halo crown with the v17 head's controlled powerful design; it must still read as an upgraded combined head. Symmetrical underlying helmet architecture in perspective, no organic lion head, no new giant extra horns, no helmet copying from v18.

4. CORRECT KNEE DRILLS. Each drill is bolted to the FRONT face of its own knee with a concentric orange/steel mount. Its axis follows that knee and foot's actual forward/toe direction, slightly forward/down, never sideways across the body. In the existing braced stance the viewer-left near knee drill points diagonally toward the LOWER-LEFT foreground; the viewer-right knee drill points toward the LOWER-RIGHT foreground and may be more foreshortened. They do not both point to image-right, do not point inward at each other and do not emerge from the knee's side. Preserve both original conical drill tools and all tracked shin armor.

5. SMALL BOMBER COLOR REFINEMENT. Retain the established orange/ivory family. Break up the large dull neutral-gray aircraft upper surface into soft matte ivory outer panels and a restrained slate-blue graphite central/deep panel system; orange on the compact chest nose, leading-edge segments and small markings. No glowing high-white surfaces, no reflective PBR, no full gray/black airplane. Use the same painted material language and hard cel shadow bands as the body. Keep lower body and train/fist identity colors consistent.

Clean confident animation key-art linework and crisp color planes. No new guns, no extra train sections, no auras, no photorealistic render. Full-body mechanical connections must be legible, with real clearance at wing roots.
